Question: Which of the following statements are true?

A. Alkali metals have a high ionization potential and a high electron affinity
B. Halogens have a high ionization potential and a high electron affinity
C. In one period, the atomic radius increases from left to right
D. Metals tend to be on the right of the periodic table, nonmetals tend to be on the left
E. The electronegativity falls from right to left in one period
F. Within a group, the atomic radius increases

Thought: I will evaluate each statement based on principles of chemistry.

A. Alkali metals (Group 1) typically have low ionization energies and low electron affinities, not high. This statement is false.
B. Halogens (Group 17) have high electron affinities as they tend to gain electrons easily, and they have relatively high ionization energies compared to other groups. This statement is true.
C. Within a period, atomic radius generally decreases from left to right due to increasing nuclear charge pulling electrons closer. This statement is false.
D. Metals are on the left side and center of the periodic table, while nonmetals are on the right. This statement is false.
E. Electronegativity generally increases from left to right across a period. This statement is false.
F. Within a group, the atomic radius increases as you move down due to the addition of electron shells. This statement is true.

Based on this evaluation, the true statements are B and F.
